questions.question: What characterises a first-person narrator?
options: The story is told with "I", giving an intimate but subjective view
The narrator knows everything about all characters
The narrator never appears in the story
The story has no narrator at all
questions.explanation: A first-person narrator ("I") gives intimacy and subjectivity — and may even be unreliable.

questions.question: What is the difference between third-person limited and third-person omniscient narration?
options: Limited follows one character's perspective; omniscient knows everything about everyone
Limited is used only in poems
Omniscient means the narrator is a character in the story
questions.explanation: Third-person limited stays with one character's thoughts, while an omniscient narrator has a complete, all-knowing overview.

questions.question: In the STEAL method for indirect characterisation, what does the A stand for?
questions.explanation: STEAL stands for Speech, Thoughts, Effect on others, Actions and Looks — ways an author shows character indirectly.

questions.question: What is a "dynamic" character?
options: A character who changes during the story
A character who is always physically active
questions.explanation: A dynamic character undergoes change or development, while a static character remains the same throughout.

questions.question: A story about a character battling a snowstorm illustrates which conflict type?
questions.explanation: A struggle against weather or the natural world is a Person vs. Nature conflict.
